Read [LLM-DISCLAIMER](docs/LLM-DISCLAIMER.md) first.

Materialize hardened, SHA-pinned GitHub Actions workflows from a small
`.actlith` registry.

Most repositories copy their `ci.yml` from the last one, and the copies
drift: a comment here, a job name there, a `timeout-minutes` nobody
carried over, an action pinned by tag in one place and by SHA in another.
actlith replaces the copies with a few rows in one file. Each row names a
workflow *kind* (`gate`, `build`, `update-pins`, `upstream`) and the few
values that differ between repositories; `actlith gen` writes the
workflow, and `actlith gen --check` fails when the file on disk no longer
matches.

```text
## workflows
id|kind|systems|cache|args
ci|gate|-|my-cachix-cache|-
```

That row becomes `.github/workflows/ci.yml`: the [hk](https://hk.jdx.dev)
gate on Linux x86, Linux arm and macOS, with nix installed and the cachix
cache wired in. Every workflow actlith writes is hardened the same way,
with no option to turn it off:

- `permissions: contents: read` at the top; a job widens only what it needs.
- Every action pinned to a full commit SHA, with its version in a comment.
- `persist-credentials: false` on checkout, unless the job pushes.
- A `concurrency` group per workflow and ref, and `timeout-minutes` on
  every job.
- No `${{ }}` inside `run:`; values reach shell through `env:`.

Every generated workflow passes `actionlint` and `zizmor` with no findings
in actlith's own test suite, so a change that would break either fails
here, not in your repository.

actlith is the GitHub Actions counterpart of
[pklith](https://github.com/pr0d1r2/pklith): pklith decides *what* the
gate checks, actlith decides *where and when* CI runs it.

## Status

Early: 0.1.0 is the first release, and the interface may still change.
The core loop works, and this repository's own CI is generated by it
([`.actlith`](.actlith) renders
[`.github/workflows/ci.yml`](.github/workflows/ci.yml)).

- `actlith gen [--check]`: write each row's workflow and the scripts its
  kind runs; `--check` writes nothing and names every stale or missing
  file.
- `actlith check`: every file in `.github/workflows/` is either generated
  by a row or listed as hand-written, with a reason.
- `actlith detect` and `actlith seed --init`: propose rows from the files
  a repository already has, and write a first `.actlith`.
- `actlith import FILE...`: print the row that renders an existing
  workflow exactly, or say where no kind matches.
- `actlith report [--format text|json|md]`: workflows, the runners each
  uses, every pinned action and every secret a workflow reads.
- `actlith pin [--dry-run]`: resolve action tags to commit SHAs through
  the GitHub API. It is the only command that uses the network.

Exit status: 0 ok, 1 a finding, 2 usage, unreadable input or a refused row.
Every message names its fix.

## Install

From crates.io, with Rust 1.95 or newer:

```sh
cargo install actlith
```

With nix, run it from the flake, or add `packages.<system>.default` to
your dev shell:

```sh
nix run github:pr0d1r2/actlith -- --help
```

To build the latest `main` instead:

```sh
cargo install --git https://github.com/pr0d1r2/actlith actlith
```

## Quick start

```sh
actlith detect            # rows proposed from your flake.nix and flake.lock
actlith seed --init       # write them to .actlith (never over an existing one)
actlith gen               # write .github/workflows/*.yml
actlith check             # every workflow file is accounted for
```

Then add `actlith gen --check` and `actlith check` to your gate, so a hand
edit to a generated file, or a workflow nobody declared, fails the commit.
[Integration](docs/INTEGRATION.md) walks through it, including moving an
existing repository with workflows of its own.
